preconditions.description: Input constraints: n is the number of sets (1 ≤ n ≤ 10000), k is the rank (1 ≤ k ≤ 100).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= m for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split())
postconditions.description: All integers in the n sets are within the range [1, m], where m is the minimal possible value printed on the first line.
The output consists of exactly n + 1 lines: the first line is m, followed by n lines of four integers each.
Each of the n sets contains exactly four distinct integers.

postconditions.expression: all(set(line.split()) == set(line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each set contains four distinct integers (no duplicates).

postconditions.expression: all(all(k == gcd(int(a), int(b)) for a in line.split() for b in line.split() if a != b) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: For every pair of distinct integers in each set, their gcd equals k.

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(x) not in set.union(*[set(line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:i-1]]) for x in line.split()) for i, line in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()[1:], 1))
postconditions.description: No integer is used in more than one set (all sets are disjoint).
The first line of the output is the minimal possible m.

candidate_issues.instruction: Fix the duplicate-checking logic in Q4 (it is redundant and incorrect). The expression should verify distinctness by comparing the length of the set to the length of the list (not comparing the set to itself).

Fix the disjointness check in Q6. The current expression is overly complex and incorrect. It should verify that no integer appears in more than one set by collecting all integers from previous sets and checking that no integer in the current set is in that collection.

Add a postcondition to ensure that the minimal m is indeed achievable with the given sets. The task requires that m is the minimal possible value, but the contract does not explicitly verify that the solution is valid (i.e., that the sets are of rank k and disjoint).
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Calculate the minimum m that makes it possible and print one possible solution.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the sets are of rank k. The current Q5 checks gcd for all pairs, but it does not explicitly enforce that the sets are of rank k (i.e., all pairs must have gcd exactly k). The expression is correct, but the task requires this as a core requirement, so it should be explicitly stated in the contract.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Define S to be of rank k if and only if for all pairs of distinct elements s_i, s_j from S, gcd(s_i, s_j) = k.
